object_description: dominant three-story building volume with a folded roof
design_condition: The volume extends the existing access axis into the open space and occupies the plain without altering the terrain, but breaks the larger green area, dominates the complex, and forms problematic courtyard relationships with nearby housing.

positive.statement: The authors treat the existing architecture with respect and keep structural interventions minimal.
The cluster concept for four classes is exciting and pedagogically promising.
The interior architectural attitude is self-confident and easy to imagine.
The transparent, bright room concept promises a friendly learning atmosphere.
The low intervention in the existing buildings helps relieve the gray-energy balance.

negative.statement: The three-story volume is dominant and obscures the existing school complex.
The building weakens the clarity of the existing architecture through difficult-to-assign facade language.
The new organization breaks the neighborhood opening and reduces the quality of the living space.
The courtyard interpretation is considered incorrect and the outside space appears listless.
The basic level lacks a direct connection to the ground floor and outside space.
The distribution of students between the two buildings is unequal.
The large volume and complex statics make the project expensive.
